# The mesh-quality door: one verdict, and the meshes it is measured on

*Gap:* `GAP-CAD-D1-MESH-QUALITY-LIB`. *Generated by* `python tools/mesh_quality_door.py` at 2026-11-15T08:55:53Z -- every number below is injected from `artifacts/mesh_quality_door/results.json`, none is transcribed by hand. *Verdict:* **PASS**.

## 1. What the door is

`tensorcad.meshquality.door.admit` composes the three gates the library already shipped separately -- shell topology (watertight / edge- and vertex-manifold / winding / outward / genus), the per-element `DEFAULT_GATE`, and the OpenFOAM interior-face non-orthogonality -- into one verdict whose failures still name the threshold, the cell kind and the margin. It adds no measure and no threshold of its own.

The interior-face measure is applied to every volume kind the library can gate --
`tet`, `hex`, `prism`, `pyramid` (`door.CELL_KINDS_WITH_INTERNAL_FACES`). Prisms and
pyramids were added after this report was first generated, because skipping a kind makes
the verdict read PASS for a measure that was never taken; the closed-form evidence for the
two new kinds is in `docs/mesh_quality_prism_pyramid.md` §5a, and it uses the same 70 deg
default. A mesh that has no interior face for a kind it contains fails that check with
"no internal faces", which is the pre-existing policy for a single tet or hex.

## 5. Baseline

`docs/meshquality/door_baseline.json` was recomputed and compared on all 9 cases at relative tolerance `1e-12`. The baseline is regenerated in memory on every run and never read back into the report, so a hand-edited baseline cannot buy a pass; `--bless` is the only way to move it and it lands as a reviewed data edit.

## 6. Notes, limits, applicability

* The upstream differential (``vtk``/``gmsh``/``meshmagick``) is **not** repeated here: those packages have no wheel on this host, and `tools/mesh_quality_crosscheck.py` already records that per run. This door's differential is closed-form plus regression.
* The gate thresholds are policy, not measurement: a PASS means the mesh is inside the declared limits, not that a solver will be accurate on it. `docs/mesh_quality_gate_power.md` measures that second, weaker claim and reports FAIL.
* `sliver_patch` and `hex_inverted` are controls: they exist to prove the door closes. If either starts passing, the door has stopped being a door.

## 7. Errors against the references

Worst closed-form relative deviation over 8 comparisons: `1.337e-16`. All are below `3%`, and below the `1e-12` this door enforces; the quiet reason is that the volume cases are rational, so the only error source is floating-point evaluation of `det^(2/3)`, `atan` and the floating Jacobian of the isoparametric map.
